newsitem.title: FRANCE: L'Oreal stock rebounds on results.
newsitem.headline: L'Oreal stock rebounds on results.

text.p: Shares in L'Oreal rebounded on Friday after the company issued first-half results confirming a cautious profit growth forecast which had knocked the shares for the two previous days.
Shares in L'Oreal were up 1.69 percent at 1,804 francs at 0920 GMT, recouping slightly more than half their two-day loss.

L'Oreal reported on Thursday that first-half pre-tax profit rose 12.1 percent to 3.09 billion francs. It predicted a similar rise in pre-tax profit for the year but signalled a slower rise in net profit, although it said net profit would grow faster than last year's 8.3 percent gain.
Most analysts had been counting on an increase above 12 percent and were disappointed by a wire report issued earlier this week containing the forecast issued in the group's first-half results.

An analyst said on Friday that the results showing a slight strengthening in the operating margin to 11.4 percent in the first half of 1996 from 11.1 percent in the 1995 first-half and a good third-quarter sales trend.
The disappointing factors for the year -- higher tax and financial expense from its Jade and Maybelline acquisitions last year -- are non-operating items, he said.
Traders said the group may also be benefitting from the boost given to dollar stocks by the U.S. currency's strength.
